key_insight: Cavity emission from two coupled qubits can be used to reconstruct the spectral density of correlated longitudinal noise, revealing how noise correlations affect quantum hardware.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical diagnostic for characterizing correlated errors in qubit-cavity systems, which is valuable for fault-tolerant quantum computing and error-correction design.
method: Model two cavity-coupled qubits subject to correlated longitudinal noise.
Analyze cavity emission for white, quasi-static, and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise.
Use averaging over noise realizations or convolution-theorem-based inversion to recover the noise correlation spectral density.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that reconstruction is possible from cavity emission by averaging over many noise realizations, with distinct scaling behavior confirmed for white versus quasi-static noise.
watch_item: Accurate reconstruction depends on knowing the frequency spectrum or on reliable inversion from emission data, and averaging over many noise realizations may be required.
paper_title: Reconstruction of the noise correlation spectral density from the cavity emission in a two-qubit system
